message:
docs(observe): what an operator has to set, and what must not be moved

The previous pass said the change needs a server-app update. It did not say
what someone actually types, which is the part they will be looking for at
the moment the thing does not work.

Two switches, and only two: REMOTE60_DIR_OBSERVE_PORT and
REMOTE60_DIR_OBSERVE_HOST. Behind TLS the first is effectively required --
an https client with no advertisement refuses rather than dialling 444 --
and the second is not validated by the server, so a wrong value is refused
by the client and recorded instead of quietly working.

The reverse-proxy half: nine flat paths, no rewrite, and
client_max_body_size at least 512KB, because the log route's limit is
512 KiB while every other body is capped at 16 KiB. A proxy that blocks the
larger one loses logs and nothing else, so the symptom is an absence rather
than an error.

And the sentence this exists to prevent someone writing: the UDP ports do
not go behind 443. Observation and relay are UDP and do not traverse a
reverse proxy. Reading "put it all on 443" and removing those forwards
kills the product -- the host never completes a heartbeat, so it never
appears in a list, and the relay has no path at all.

For whoever reads the logs afterwards: a 409 naming an observation is not an
authentication failure. The client repairs it itself, once. A 401 is the
token being gone and does re-register, and the two must not be read as the
same event.

The numbers here were read out of the code in this repository. The live NAS
configuration was not looked at -- this work never connected to it -- and
the section says so rather than implying the deployment was checked.

Also cross-referenced from history: the loose port read at
directory_client.cpp:451 is still not fixed. The strict reader added in this
work went into the advertisement parser, not there.
